test: e2e/check-dpr.spec.ts :: committing a Draw stroke preserves the live HiDPI preview pixels
evidence: DrawToolArea.tsx (preview) draws on tool-overlay-canvas which has HiDPI backing store (canvas.width = CSS_width * DPR) and context transform (setTransform(DPR, 0, 0, DPR, 0, 0)). The stroke is rendered via ctx.stroke() at device pixel resolution.

draw.ts creator (commit) creates OffscreenCanvas(size.width, size.height) using CSS pixel dimensions only (line 107). No backingScale parameter is passed to CreatorToolParams (toolProcessors.ts:40-42). The stroke is rendered at 1x resolution via ctx.stroke().
layer-utils.ts:320 calls processor.imageProcessor({ size: pos }) with CSS-pixel pos. The creator receives no DPR information.

drawLayersToCanvas (layer-renderer.ts:537) creates staging canvas at HiDPI via resizeCanvas(..., backingScale=DPR). The layer's 1x tmpCanvas is drawn to 2x staging canvas with imageSmoothingEnabled=false (nearest-neighbor upscale) in drawEvaluatedPresentation (presentation-evaluator.ts:317).

Test captures preview as workspaceCanvas + overlayCanvas at full 2x backing store resolution (lines 136-156), then compares against workspaceCanvas after commit (lines 162-169). The preview stroke was drawn at 2x; the committed stroke was drawn at 1x then nearest-neighbor upscaled to 2x — producing different anti-aliasing and pixel values.
rootCause: The Draw tool's creator (draw.ts) creates a 1x OffscreenCanvas in CSS pixels, ignoring the device pixel ratio. The live preview draws on a HiDPI canvas (2x backing store + 2x context transform) at device pixel resolution. On commit, the 1x stroke bitmap is nearest-neighbor upscaled to 2x for display, producing different pixels than the 2x native preview stroke.
proposal: Add backingScale to CreatorToolParams (toolProcessors.ts), thread DPR from useLayer.ts (useDevicePixelRatio) through buildLayerFromTool -> createLayerSource -> creator, and update draw.ts creator to create HiDPI OffscreenCanvas (width*backingScale, height*backingScale) with setTransform(backingScale, 0, 0, backingScale, 0, 0) so the commit renders at the same device-pixel resolution as the preview.
